david.name: David
david.title: David (Dawud)
david.dict: He kills Goliath and is given kingship and wisdom (2:251). God gives him the Psalms (4:163, 17:55); the mountains and the birds sing God's praise with him, and iron is made soft for him to make coats of mail (21:79-80, 34:10-11). Two disputants test him with a case about one ewe and ninety-nine, and he asks forgiveness (38:21-25); the Quran does not tell the story of Bathsheba.

desert-arabs.name: The desert Arabs
desert-arabs.title: The desert Arabs
desert-arabs.dict: The nomads around Medina. Some make excuses to stay behind from the campaigns; they are "the most steeped in disbelief and hypocrisy" (9:97), yet some of them believe (9:99). "Say, You have not believed; but say, We have submitted" (49:14).

dhul-kifl.name: Dhul-Kifl
dhul-kifl.title: Dhul-Kifl
dhul-kifl.dict: Named twice, in lists of the steadfast and the outstanding (21:85, 38:48), with nothing told of him. Some identify him with Ezekiel, and Talal Itani's translation says Ezekiel; others with other figures. The Quran does not say who he was.

dhul-qarnayn.name: Dhul-Qarnayn
dhul-qarnayn.title: Dhul-Qarnayn
dhul-qarnayn.dict: "The one of the two horns": a ruler given power on the earth, who travels to the setting and the rising of the sun and builds a barrier of iron against Gog and Magog (18:83-98). Who he was is disputed; he has often been identified with Alexander the Great, and by some with Cyrus.
